I went today because I had booked an appointment online for teeth cleaning. The website stated that I needed to present myself with proof of appointment by 4:00 PM. So I arrived early to proceed as instructed on the website. Upon arrival, I was a little confused because the security guard said I had to wait until 4:00 PM. The security guard was lovely, spoke well, and gave excellent advice. However, due to the confusion stemming from the website's instructions (as previously mentioned), I asked the counter staff again. The staff told me to go up to the 3rd floor to book an appointment (I already told them I had booked online and this was my first time there. They seemed confused and thought I hadn't booked an appointment yet. The staff member was very nice and spoke well). So I went up to the 3rd floor. I met a female staff member—I'm not sure of her position—who asked why I was up there. I explained, and she clarified that I had to wait until 4:00 PM. It wasn't time yet; the staff were cleaning and tidying up. She asked me to wait downstairs. She was polite during the conversation, but perhaps her tone wasn't perfect. I understand, and I probably overthought it. I didn't hold a grudge and thanked her. But as soon as I turned around to wait for the elevator, before I could even step inside... The officer sighed loudly and spoke in a local dialect, complaining about a headache and slightly grumbling to another officer. I think this behavior is completely inappropriate. Please improve this, as I am certain I spoke to you politely. Even if you were annoyed, this is a mistake in the website's instructions and the officer's responsibility. I would like Center 45 to correct the text on the website. "Within 16:00" refers to the time period before and until the end time of 16:00. If you want people to wait until 4:00, it should say "from 16:00 onwards" to be correct. Please correct this.

This is my third time using their services because I need continuous wound cleaning from a cat bite. Previously, I went to a well-known private hospital in Ramkhamhaeng, and on the first day, I was charged over 10,000 baht because I needed serum injections, a tetanus booster, and the first rabies shot. My insurance completely covered it. So I tried continuing treatment at Romklao Public Health Center to see how it would go. My intention was that if it wasn't good, I'd go back to using my insurance for outpatient care at a private hospital. In short, it's excellent! The nurses are very skilled^^ They clean the wound well and even drain the pus. The first one or two times I went to the private hospital, they cleaned the wound like I would at home, and it was still painful at night. I wanted to share that you can try using public health services near your home. Romklao Public Health Center 45 has excellent service, the staff are caring, polite, and very kind.

I went to this dental clinic (Center 45) to have a tooth extracted, but I found it incredibly painful. I was so tense during the extraction that my hands were shaking, even though the tooth was already loose and about to fall out. When I got home, I kept thinking about why it hurt so much. I felt like the dentist didn't give me enough anesthetic. Usually, after anesthetic injections, my mouth is almost numb. But at this center, it wasn't as numb as at a regular clinic because I paid for it, so they get more numbness. In short, the dentist didn't give enough anesthetic, which is why it hurt. Normally, extractions at a regular clinic aren't painful at all. If you're going there, tell your dentist to give you more anesthetic, otherwise you'll be trembling like me.

text:
Today, May 13, 2024, I woke up with a headache, slight fever, and a slight cough. I was scared, so I grabbed an ATK test kit and tested myself. The result: two lines! I am 69 years old and have a pre-existing condition of cerebral artery stenosis. Because I wanted to get COVID-19 medication, I went to this center at 6:30 AM. When I arrived, I said I was there to get tested for COVID-19. The volunteers told me to sit in the garden. I sat and waited until after 8:30 AM, but I was still not called, even though I was the only one waiting for COVID-19 testing. I had a headache, dizziness, and blurred vision, so I had to go ask for help. Because of the severe headache, I saw a screening nurse. She asked if I had a test result. I replied that I didn't, that I just wanted to get tested for COVID-19. She said that if I didn't have proof of a test, she wouldn't treat me. So I showed her the picture of my test I took that morning. The nurse said that it was definitely COVID-19 and I didn't need to see a doctor; I could just get medication. I was happy, thinking I would be able to go home soon. It was around 8:45 AM, but the nurse said, "You can go home or wait. You'll get the medication around 11 AM." They said I had to go through the system first.
We were confused about what system we were in, we didn't even see a doctor or get examined. And why did we have to get medication at 11 am? Actually, I was the only one with COVID, they should have given me the medication and sent me home quickly so I wouldn't spread the infection to other people, especially the elderly in the area.
In short, I'm very confused. If they had asked me from the beginning if I had a test kit with results, and if I didn't, they wouldn't have tested me, and I could have gone somewhere else. But instead, I waited until late, almost time to see the doctor, before they finally asked. How do they even work? Giving them one star is already too much. In summary, I received treatment at Bamrasnaradura Infectious Diseases Institute, Nonthaburi.
